question: On this Apple-Silicon host, is there a native official Blender 5.2 Linux worker route, and if not, is an x64-emulated disposable worker sufficiently identified to deserve a later runtime canary without being mislabeled as production containment?

officialNativeArm64.acceptWhen: official release index lists the exact frozen Linux arm64 filename and checksum manifest binds it to a SHA-256

officialX64Emulated.acceptForLaterCanaryWhen: official x64 filename, byte count and SHA-256 match; host and Docker architectures match the frozen ARM64 identity; disk admission is ACCEPTED; a separately built worker image is digest pinned

minimumChecks: Blender executable bytes match the official x64 artifact provenance chain
factory startup, disable-autoexec and offline-mode remain active
only the output mount accepts writes
effective UID and GID are non-root
PID, memory, CPU and wall-time breach receipts are captured
timeout reaches SIGKILL after the frozen grace period when SIGTERM is ignored
failed, timed-out or cancelled outputs are never promotable
a real minimal Blender compile or render receipt is produced

frozenAnalyzerAttacks: fabricate an official Linux arm64 artifact
change the official x64 byte count
remove a required Docker security option
claim that a container or Blender process executed
mark B40 complete before a separate preregistration

decisionRules.architecturePreflightSupportRuntimeBlock: all frozen gates and all 15 attacks pass; native route is rejected; emulated route is identified but the real host remains below disk reserve; runtime operations executed equals zero
decisionRules.nativeOfficialRouteAvailable: the exact frozen official Linux arm64 filename is present and bound by the official checksum manifest; this outcome contradicts the preregistered current observation and requires a new protocol
decisionRules.runInvalid: runtime, spec, preregistration ancestry, source identity, probe allowlist, attack count or evidence self-hash differs

nonClaims: B39 does not launch Blender, create or run a container, build or pull an image, or download the Blender archive
Absence from the official 5.2.0 release index is not a claim that Blender cannot be compiled from source for Linux arm64
The x64 artifact being identifiable does not prove it runs correctly under Colima emulation
Docker security options being present does not prove containment against kernel, daemon, parser, GPU or denial-of-service vulnerabilities
No Eevee, EGL, software rasterizer, Cycles, performance, determinism or output-equivalence claim
No production backend selection or promotion claim
No disk-reserve override and no automatic cleanup
